summary: Summation No. 35, the final issue of the series, covers August 1948 (statistics mostly for June-July) and carries a Review of the Third Occupation Year (1 September 1947 - 31 August 1948). Politically the month is dominated by the Ashida cabinet's cabinet order and planned revision of the National Public Service Law following MacArthur's July letter, labor unrest on the railways, argument over dissolving the Diet and a proposed centrist league, the Illegal Transactions Investigation Committee hearings (Nishio acquitted, Nakasone sentenced), the Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damage to textile mills, and MacArthur's address at the inauguration of the Republic of Korea. Economic parts cover SCAP's removal of export controls (15-18 August), a sterling-area trade plan, price stabilization, hoarded goods, the Reconstruction Finance Bank, holding-company dissolution and reparations shipments. Long statistical sections give production of coal, metals, chemicals, textiles, power, communications, labor, trade, prices, finance, science, patents, health and education, useful for quantifying recovery. The appendix surveys the third Occupation year.
highlights: MacArthur addressed the 15 August inauguration of the Republic of Korea in Seoul before President Rhee, calling Korea's division an artificial barrier to be torn down.

A July cabinet order denied government employees strikes and collective bargaining; a Cabinet interpretation followed 11 August, and Shikoku absenteeism cancelled 118 trains on 16 August with 956 discharged.
Former deputy prime minister Nishio was acquitted 27 August, while Nakasone was sentenced to four years on 31 August in the Army Uniform Case.
SCAP authorized elimination of major Japanese Government export controls on 15-18 August, letting foreign buyers deal directly with sellers; a sterling-area trade plan was set at 242 million dollars.
The Holding Company Liquidation Commission issued its first final reorganization order on 22 August, splitting Japan Soda Company into six companies.
The Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damaged 686 of 1,774 textile mills; the Reconstruction Finance Bank was to lend about 1.12 billion yen for repairs.
Japanese B encephalitis struck about 4,100 people with 219 deaths by 28 August, and equine encephalomyelitis killed 522 horses.
The review of the third Occupation year shows the industrial production index rising from 43.1 to 59.9, with Japan's cumulative trade deficit near 822.8 million dollars.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Archive cover, notice that this is the final issue of the Summation, title page, table of contents and list of 108 numbered charts and tables.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of August 1948: no change in SCAP organization, then political, economic and social items including MacArthur at Seoul, trade controls lifted 15 August, and encephalitis epidemics.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: No change occurred in the non-military organization of GHQ SCAP during August.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Digest of MacArthur's Seoul address, constitutional revision, the Public Service Law debate, Diet dissolution, centrist realignment, court decisions, dissolved ultranationalist groups, public safety figures and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of rail unrest, trade controls lifted 15 August, food rations, finance, property control and antitrust, alongside agriculture, mining, industrial output, power, communications, labor and science items.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of encephalitis epidemics, public assistance increases, repatriation of 44,400, the Board of Education Law, university reorganization, and religion and press items.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics (Public Service Law order, Diet dissolution dispute, corruption hearings, purge), public safety, and legal affairs including war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: MacArthur and Ashida messages, constitutional revision study, Public Service Law cabinet order, Diet dissolution dispute, party maneuvers, local elections, corruption hearings, purge cases and economic policy statements.

sections.title: Supreme Commander's Statement to Republic of Korea
sections.summary: MacArthur's 15 August Seoul address to President Rhee: friendship since 1882, Korea's artificial division, and defense of liberty.

sections.title: Prime Minister's Message on Anniversary of Defeat
sections.summary: Ashida's 15 August anniversary message cited improving living conditions and falling inflation, and urged a middle path and peace-loving reconstruction.

sections.title: Constitutional Revision Proposals
sections.summary: Diet leaders agreed 20 August on a joint committee to study revision; six topics listed, including the Emperor's ceremonial role and Diet conflicts.

sections.title: Political Developments: National Public Service Law Discussion
sections.summary: Cabinet order banning government employees' strikes and collective bargaining; labor and Communist reaction, Cabinet interpretation of 11 August, a social democratic seven-point plan and cabinet disagreements.

sections.title: Problem of Diet Dissolution
sections.summary: Government parties split on dissolving the Diet: Ashida wants delay to year end; Katayama and left-wing Social Democrats want a November election.

sections.title: Prime Minister's Address to Foreign Correspondents
sections.summary: Ashida's 27 August speech to foreign correspondents on food, clothing, slowing inflation, labor, political stability and middle-of-the-road policy.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Debate over a Middle Course Political League; positions of the Democratic, Social Democratic, People's Cooperative and Democratic Liberal parties, plus minor parties including the Communists.

sections.title: Local Government
sections.summary: Recall of a Saitama village mayor upheld on a tied recount; an independent was elected governor in an August prefectural election.

sections.title: Illegal Transactions Investigations
sections.summary: Nishio acquitted; Nakasone sentenced in the Army Uniform Case; Kano case, Area Disposal and coal-mine bribery hearings; new charges against Miki and Kitamura.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Ultranationalist groups dissolved in August; 377,788 screened and 201,333 purged by month end; indictments for purge violations.

sections.title: Economic Plans and Policies
sections.summary: Government pledge to the ESB ten-point policy, financial reorganization plan, wage dispute over the National Personnel Authority, payroll cuts, and party anti-inflation and reconstruction programs.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Hoarded goods (5.95 million yen recovered in July), black-market and bribery cases, June crime statistics, prison population, fires, and transfer of offshore policing to the Maritime Safety Board.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Supreme Court caseload, domestic relations court, 70 suspects apprehended and 713 tried to date; seven trials in the period, two death sentences; IMTFE in recess.

sections.title: Part III: Business
sections.summary: Fourteen economic sections of production, trade, price, finance and science statistics, from agriculture and coal to textiles, labor, exports, reparations and patents.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Agricultural cooperative program and cabinet orders, Kanto Plain soil survey, June marine catch down to 150,018 tons, tuna export rejections, petroleum allocations and whaling.

sections.title: Agricultural cooperatives and administration
sections.summary: Dissolution of agricultural associations and three August cabinet orders on property transfers to cooperatives.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: Smaller sardine and mackerel catches, spoilage from lack of ice, a new purse seiner, August fuel allocations and 2,210 tons of whale products.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: August coal output 3,542,000 tons (down about 300,000), deliveries, stockpiles, lignite, crude oil drilling and strike effects, and June mineral output with mercury up.

sections.title: Coal, oil and mining industry
sections.summary: Coal deliveries of 2,669,000 tons in July, district production, stockpiles, lignite, crude oil and mine production.

sections.title: Section 3. Industrial Raw Materials
sections.summary: July coke 264,112 tons; pig iron and rolled steel at postwar peaks; cement down 12 percent; light metals, copper, zinc, petroleum refining, chemicals, salt and paper figures.

sections.title: Coke and metal industries
sections.summary: Coke production, deliveries and stocks; iron, steel, aluminum, copper, zinc, tin and ferroalloys; petroleum products.

sections.title: Cement, chemicals, salt, pulp and paper
sections.summary: Cement down on coal and transport shortages; 21 of 28 chemicals up; caustic soda at postwar peak; salt output up 50.6 percent; paper at postwar peak.

sections.title: Section 4. Machinery, Equipment and Construction
sections.summary: Machine tools, bearings, textile machinery, rolling stock, electrical and communications equipment, truck output of 1,388, coal miners' housing and building permits.

sections.title: Section 5. Manufactured Goods
sections.summary: June cigarettes up 12.3 percent, plus food processing, brewing, glass, rubber, leather, watches, sewing machines, ship completions and the Soviet tug contract.

sections.title: Section 6. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damage to mills, cotton imports, raw silk at a postwar peak of 11,521 bales, rayon, wool, bast fibers and knit goods.

sections.title: Earthquake damage
sections.summary: Survey recommends 1.514 billion yen for repairs; 686 of 1,774 mills damaged; Reconstruction Finance Bank to lend 1.12 billion yen.

sections.title: Cotton
sections.summary: Cotton imports rose to 43.9 million pounds in July; spinners' supplies, yarn and fabric production and machinery.

sections.title: Silk
sections.summary: July raw silk output reached a postwar peak of 11,531 bales, mostly 20/22 denier; tested silk fell to 2,124 bales, and silk fabric output dropped 316,000 square yards amid yarn shortages and earthquake-area mill losses.

sections.title: Artificial fibers and wool
sections.summary: Rayon pulp imports and caustic soda bottleneck limit rayon yarn and fabric; raw wool imported from Australia and South America.

sections.title: Hard and bast fibers, spun and reprocessed materials, knit goods, sundries, dyeing
sections.summary: Hard and bast fiber stocks rose to 20,520,000 pounds with Indian jute arrivals; rope output rose 1,841,000 pounds, jute yarn jumped to 522,000 pounds, and knit underwear for export fell to 181,319 dozen.

sections.title: Section 7. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Shikoku railway unrest, 519.9 million passengers, 17 August directive for Japan to assume port operations, coastwise shipping, July electric power of 2.94 billion kWh and gas industry figures.

sections.title: Railways and water transportation
sections.summary: Communist-led absenteeism on Shikoku with 956 discharged; 17 August directive on port and terminal operations; coastal and foreign cargo.

sections.title: Electric power and gas
sections.summary: July electric power generation was about 2.94 billion kWh, 8.5 percent below July 1947; hydroelectric supplied 2,775 million kWh while thermal fell 65.5 percent to 71 million; stream flow ran 21 percent above June.

sections.title: Section 8. Communications
sections.summary: 1,386,084 telephones after the Telephone Bond Law, 6,858,814 licensed radio listeners, radio frequency changes, and postal volume drop after the 11 July rate rise.

sections.title: Section 9. Labor
sections.summary: Labor rally against the Ashida cabinet, union statistics, Hokkaido and Imperial Oil disputes, wage increases for Occupation workers, labor standards inspections, and women and minors.

sections.title: Labor relations and disputes
sections.summary: Hokkaido railway walkout, coal wage agreement, electric power dispute, Imperial Oil mediation and Toho studio eviction.

sections.title: Employment and unemployment
sections.summary: Employment Security Advisory Committee, coal mine employment recheck, vocational training and unemployment insurance.

sections.title: Section 10. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Export controls eliminated, sterling-area trade plan for 242 million dollars, 10 million dollars of cotton contracts, Siam talks, and a first-half deficit of 271 million dollars.

sections.title: Section 11. Price and Distribution
sections.summary: Record summer vegetable harvest, three more price stabilization groups, textile prices up about 90 percent, consumer price index 342.9, incentive goods and surplus Army cigarettes.

sections.title: Section 12. Finance
sections.summary: Economic Investigation Board created 1 August; notes in circulation 264 billion yen; Reconstruction Finance Bank plan; 18 control associations closed; first prison terms for tax evasion.

sections.title: Section 13. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Attorney-General to liquidate dissolved organizations, looted property status, holding company orders, Fair Trade Commission filings and machine tool shipments to claimants.

sections.title: Section 14. Science and Technology
sections.summary: New Industrial Technique Management Council, Japanese physicists' travel to Princeton, FEC access to Japanese processes, patent statistics, and a background survey of Japan's climate.

sections.title: Patents and standards
sections.summary: Forty Japanese Standards issued in July, FEC technical access order of 6 August, and patent and utility-model statistics.

sections.title: Climate of Japan
sections.summary: Describes Japan's climate: eight storm types from China (South Mongolia 21.2 a year), typhoons peaking July–October, three forest zones, rice and mandarin limits near 27°N, sweet potato acreage 276,000 ha in 1947, and the late April 1947 frost near Tokyo.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare (encephalitis, repatriation, public assistance), and education, religion, cultural resources and media, including the Board of Education Law.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Japanese B encephalitis and equine epidemics, Fukui earthquake aid, medical supplies, narcotics, public assistance, population 80,170,815 and repatriation of 44,625.

sections.title: Medical administration and supply
sections.summary: Nursing courses, production of penicillin, DDT and X-ray equipment, veterinary and inspection data, and distribution of medical supplies.

sections.title: Narcotics, public assistance and social security
sections.summary: Narcotics handler registrations, welfare payments and new allowance rates, LARA shipments, a 40 percent medical fee increase and insurance statistics.

sections.title: Vital statistics, population and repatriation
sections.summary: June birth rate lowest since 1929; population 80,170,815; census density maps; 6,024,896 repatriated by 2 September.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teachers' union cabinet ordinance, Board of Education Law and October elections, university reorganization, textbooks, religion, press comment, the Asahi Saitama case, radio, films and SCAP libraries.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Redefined relations with the teachers' union, Board of Education Law, 219 university applications, textbooks and libraries.

sections.title: Religion, cultural resources and media of expression
sections.summary: Buddhist reform, Christian missions, press and radio themes, motion pictures and two new SCAP libraries.

sections.title: Appendix: Review of the Third Occupation Year (1 September 1947 - 31 August 1948)
sections.summary: Year-end review of 1 September 1947 to 31 August 1948: SCAP organization, economic recovery (production index 43.1 to 59.9), living conditions and democratization.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Restitution Advisory Committee established 13 April; no other organizational change during the year; chart of GHQ organization follows.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Recovery
sections.summary: Industrial production index rose from 43.1 to 59.9; coal and power, textiles, trade and sterling arrangements, transport, communications, finance, property control and reparations.

sections.title: Section 3. Living Conditions
sections.summary: Nutrition, ration distribution, housing and rents, textile distribution, wage and price inflation, disaster relief, disease campaigns, health and child welfare laws, welfare and repatriation.

sections.title: Section 4. Progress of Democratization
sections.summary: Third-year reforms: Home Ministry abolished 21 December 1947; police decentralized; 301,510 purged; party realignment; IMTFE adjourned 15 April 1948; 1,378 atrocity cases; cooperative and antitrust laws; Labor Ministry; 13,000,000 students; press censorship ended 25 July.
